get.summary: Whether a merge is waiting on this account's confirmation.
get.description:
Set when `!link` found the MXID already attached to an unclaimed account
holding data — the user is told to come back here, where the counts can
actually be shown before they agree to move anything.

200.description: Codes left, and any recovery counting down

post.summary: Stops a recovery someone started from a linked Matrix account.
post.description:
Deliberately takes [`AuthUser`], not [`VerifiedUser`]. Everything else here
is gated on a fresh passkey, but this is the *defence* against a recovery
nobody asked for — demanding a passkey to cancel would be exactly backwards
when the person cancelling may be racing a 24-hour clock on their phone.

400.description: Malformed server name or media ID

get.summary: SSE endpoint streaming real-time system events to authenticated web clients.
get.description:
Emits unnamed event-stream messages whose body carries `type` and `payload`.

The broadcast channel is process-wide, so every subscriber sees every event.
This handler is what narrows it back down: a client receives only events it
owns, matching the per-owner scoping the REST endpoints enforce.

parameters.name: completed
parameters.description:
Narrows the listing to one completion state. Omitted returns both, so
`total` counts every task — callers wanting an outstanding-work figure
must ask for `completed=false` explicitly.

BuyHoldingRequest.description:
Amounts and quantities arrive as decimal strings, never as JSON numbers —
the same reason `finance::TransactionRequest` does: a JSON number is an
IEEE-754 double by the time most clients have parsed it.

CashBalance.description:
Cash available to spend on a buy, in one currency. A missing row means a
zero balance — the same "no row until you touch it" convention as
`settings::UserSettings`.

balance_minor.description:
Never negative — enforced in `PortfolioRepository`, not the schema, the
same app-level-only convention `quantity_minor`/`avg_cost_minor` use.

owner_id.description: The owning `owner_id`. Categories are per-user, never shared.

uncategorised.description:
Entries kept but left uncategorised. Deleting a category never deletes
financial records.

CeremonyStart.description: What a browser needs to begin registering a passkey.

ceremony_id.description: Quoted back on finish, so the server can find its half of the ceremony.

options.description: The raw WebAuthn options, passed to `navigator.credentials`.

remind_before_minutes.description: Minutes before `next_due_at` to send a reminder.

remind_room_id.description:
Where to deliver that reminder. Required when the bill has no Matrix
room of its own.

remind_before_minutes.description: Minutes before `due_at` to send a reminder. Requires `due_at`.

remind_room_id.description:
Matrix room the due reminder should be delivered to. Defaults to the
task's own room; required when that is the `web` sentinel.

CurrencySummary.description:
Totals for one currency. Currencies are never combined — without a rate
source, adding EUR to JPY would produce a meaningless number.

Direction.description:
Which way the money moved.

`amount_minor` is always positive; this is what carries the sign, so a row
cannot contradict itself.

Holding.description:
One investment position: symbol, quantity, and weighted-average cost basis.

`quantity_minor` and `avg_cost_minor` are always positive integers, scaled at
[`QUANTITY_EXPONENT`] and `currency_exponent` respectively. `current_price_minor`
is `None` until the user records one — an unset price is a normal state, not
an error, so market value and unrealized P&L are computed only when it is set.

currency_exponent.description:
Decimal places for this row's currency, stored so a later change to the
currency table cannot rewrite what this row means.

note.description: A single freeform comment, most-recent-wins — not a transaction log.

MergePreview.description:
How many rows each table would contribute to a merge.

Shown to the user before they confirm, because "this will move 47 todos and
132 transactions into your account" is a decision someone should get to
make with the numbers in front of them.

PortfolioCurrencySummary.description:
Totals for one currency. Currencies are never combined — without a rate
source, adding a USD position to a JPY position produces a meaningless
number, exactly as `finance::models::CurrencySummary` documents.

cash_minor.description:
Present even for a currency with no holdings at all — a deposit with
nothing bought yet must still show up here.

market_value_minor.description: Market value of only the holdings that have a price set.

unrealized_pl_minor.description: Unrealized P&L of only the holdings that have a price set.

codes.description: Shown exactly once. The server keeps only hashes.

RecurrencePattern.description: Pattern for recurring reminders (none, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly).

RecurringBill.description: Represents a recurring bill, subscription, installment, or recurring transfer.

remind_before_minutes.description:
Minutes before `next_due_at` to send a reminder. `None` means no
reminder is wanted.

remind_room_id.description:
Matrix room the due reminder is delivered to. Defaults to the bill's own
room; required when that is the `web` sentinel.

label.description: What to call this passkey in the account's own list.

display_name.description: The name to show on this account. Display only.

invite.description: The invite secret, when the deployment requires one.

Reminder.description: A reminder stored in the database.

source_id.description:
The id of the row in that module which scheduled this reminder, so
changing or retiring that row can reschedule or cancel it.

source_kind.description: Which module scheduled this reminder, if any — see [`ReminderSource`].

total.description: Total pending reminders matching the query.

ReminderStatus.description: Status of a reminder in the database.

SessionResponse.description: Who the caller is now signed in as.

current.description: Whether this is the session making the request.

id.description:
The session's storage key. Safe to expose — it is a hash, not the
cookie, so it cannot be replayed.

to.description: End of the period, exclusive — so month boundaries do not double-count.

due_at.description:
When the task is due, stored as a real timestamp so a lead-time reminder
can be computed from it. Rendered for display only at the edges.

remind_before_minutes.description: Minutes before `due_at` to fire a reminder. `None` means no reminder.

total.description: Total rows matching the query, so clients can render page counts.

completed.description:
Narrows the listing to one completion state. Omitted returns both, so
`total` counts every task — callers wanting an outstanding-work figure
must ask for `completed=false` explicitly.

category_id.description: `None` means uncategorised, which is a valid and expected state.

category_name.description: Denormalised for reads so listing a ledger is one query, not N+1.

currency_exponent.description:
Decimal places for this row's currency, stored so a later change to the
currency table cannot rewrite what this row means.

occurred_at.description: When the money moved — not when the row was written.

sender_name.description: Display only — user-controlled, and collides across identity spaces.

TransactionRequest.description:
Amounts arrive as decimal strings, never as JSON numbers.

A JSON number is an IEEE-754 double by the time most clients have parsed it,
and `15.50` does not survive that exactly. The string is converted to minor
units by string manipulation.

occurred_at.description: When the money moved. Defaults to now.

remind_before_minutes.description: Absent leaves the lead time alone; `null` clears it; a value sets it.

UpdateReminderRequest.description:
Mirrors `CreateReminderRequest` rather than patching individual fields: the
fire time is expressed as a delay from now, exactly as at creation, so an
edit and a create mean the same thing by the same arithmetic.

UpdateSettingsRequest.description:
Both preferences are always sent together — settings are saved as a whole
row, so there is no partial-update path to get wrong.

UpdateTodoRequest.description:
A PATCH body.

The nullable fields are `Option<Option<T>>` so the three cases stay
distinguishable on the wire: absent leaves the value alone, `null` clears it,
and a value sets it. A plain `Option<T>` would make "clear the due date"
unexpressible.

account_id.description: The signed-in account. The frontend keys its caches on this.

linked_mxids.description:
Matrix identities linked to this account, if any. An empty list is the
normal state for someone who has only ever used the web UI.

UserSettings.description:
One user's display preferences, keyed by the same `owner_id` every other
ownership check uses (`AuthUser::owner_id`, the `owner_id` column).

Deliberately shared by both front doors: the SPA renders timestamps in
`timezone` and pre-selects `currency`, and the Matrix command handlers format
their HTML replies with the same two values, so a user sees one consistent
answer no matter which door they came through.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. `CNY`. Validated on write.

timezone.description: IANA zone name, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`. Validated on write.

session_cookie.name: mb_session
session_cookie.description: Session cookie set by the passkey sign-in endpoints. HttpOnly, so it is sent by the browser automatically and is not readable by JavaScript.
